body_markdown:
Building an e-commerce application used to require months of development time, a dedicated engineering team, and significant capital investment. AI app builders have changed this equation, enabling founders and small business owners to create functional online stores through conversation rather than code. Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) provide managed full-stack infrastructure for building custom product catalogs, customer accounts, and payment-enabled applications.


According to the U.S. Census Bureau, e-commerce accounted for an estimated[16.4% of total](https://www2.census.gov/retail/releases/historical/ecomm/25q4.pdf) U.S. retail sales in 2025, highlighting the importance of digital commerce for businesses. This guide examines eight AI app builders through the lens of e-commerce functionality, helping you evaluate which platform best fits your online store requirements.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **MCP connector avoids separate AI build-credit charges** : Floot connects with Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, using your existing AI subscription without separate Floot AI build credits, subject to daily action limits and connector permissions.
- **Production-ready infrastructure supports real transactions** : E-commerce apps need managed databases, authentication, payment integration, and reliable hosting.[Floot's infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) provides managed database, authentication, and hosting services, while live Stripe payments require a paid plan and connecting a Stripe account.
- **Mobile app packaging expands sales channels** : Floot supports[iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) , allowing businesses to create mobile shopping experiences without maintaining separate mobile codebases.
- **Transparent pricing improves cost visibility** : Floot offers fixed monthly plans with daily building-action allowances. Hosting beyond included allowances and optional AI features may incur additional charges.
- **Built-in SEO improves discoverability** : Optional server-side pre-rendering, metadata controls, and sitemap configuration help search engines discover and crawl product pages, although indexing and rankings are not guaranteed.


## **Understanding AI App Builders for E-commerce**


AI app builders for e-commerce translate business requirements into functional online stores through natural language conversation. Unlike traditional no-code platforms that rely on manual drag-and-drop configuration, these tools let users describe their needs and generate application code automatically.


The core requirements for e-commerce AI builders include:


- **Payment gateway integration** : Connect Stripe, PayPal, or other payment processors to support secure transactions and checkout workflows.
- **Product catalog management** : Use databases to organize inventory, pricing, product descriptions, and variants.
- **User authentication** : Enable customer account creation, secure login, and order history tracking.
- **Shopping cart functionality** : Manage cart sessions, product selections, and checkout processes.
- **Order processing** : Support fulfillment workflows, customer notifications, and order status updates through backend logic.
- **Mobile accessibility** : Provide responsive storefront designs or mobile app packaging for customers shopping on smartphones.


The platforms covered in this guide approach these requirements differently, from full-stack solutions with managed infrastructure to development environments requiring external service assembly.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Rather than replacing these AI assistants, Floot provides managed application infrastructure while the connected assistant handles development. Available building capabilities depend on the client's connector permissions.


### **Key Capabilities for E-commerce**


- **MCP connector architecture** : Build through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations using your existing AI subscription. The connector supports creating, editing, debugging, and publishing applications when the AI client provides the required tool permissions
- **Managed PostgreSQL database** : Automatic database provisioning for product catalogs, customer records, and order data with browser-based table viewing
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password login plus Google and Microsoft OAuth brokering without separate OAuth app registration
- **Payment integration support** : Built-in[Stripe payments](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) for checkout, shopping carts, and subscriptions, with other payment providers connectable through supported external APIs
- **Mobile app packaging** : Package web stores into iOS and Android apps using native mobile shells, with support for TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks through connected developer accounts
- **File storage and backend services** : Managed storage, serverless backend endpoints, and application hosting for product images, order documents, and customer-facing workflows


### **E-commerce Use Cases**


Floot handles e-commerce workflows across multiple business types. Product-based stores can manage inventory, process orders, and handle customer accounts through conversational development. Service businesses can build booking systems with payment collection. Floot can support customized marketplace workflows, with multi-vendor payment routing and seller payouts handled through additional integrations rather than its standard built-in Stripe checkout.


Floot allows businesses to build customized tools, including inventory systems, customer portals, and payment-enabled applications, without manually configuring separate hosting, database, and authentication services.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free ($0/month)** : Free to start with up to 100 build actions/day, subject to applicable account usage limits, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, 2 mobile app builds/month, a one-time $3 hosting credit, and Stripe test payments only
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, $10/month hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds/month, custom domains, and live Stripe payments with a 1% Floot fee plus Stripe processing fees
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, $25/month hosting allowance, unlimited mobile builds, and live Stripe payments with a 0% Floot fee plus Stripe processing fees


Floot's[pricing model](https://floot.com/en/pricing) combines fixed monthly subscriptions with daily building-action allowances. Prices shown are for monthly billing, with two months free on yearly billing. Connector-based building uses your existing AI subscription, while hosting beyond included allowances and optional AI features may incur additional charges. Floot AI credits are also used for image generation, in-app AI features, and Floot's optional AI agent, while standard connector-based building uses daily build actions instead.


### **Why Floot Works for E-commerce**


Floot's architecture addresses several e-commerce requirements. The platform includes[SEO controls](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) with optional server-side pre-rendering that businesses can enable to make product pages more accessible to search engine crawlers. Built-in[transactional email](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/email) supports order confirmations and shipping notifications without requiring a separate email provider, although businesses must verify a sending domain on a paid plan before delivering emails to customers.[Scheduled tasks](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/jobs) can support inventory sync, abandoned cart reminders, and reporting automation in published applications on paid Floot plans.


For businesses considering whether to build custom e-commerce solutions versus using platforms like Shopify, Floot offers an approach to[custom e-commerce workflows](https://floot.com/blog/shopify-alternative-for-custom-ecommerce-workflows-when-floot-makes-more-sense) that provides application-level customization without requiring businesses to manage the underlying infrastructure.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is an AI-powered web application builder that generates applications from natural language prompts. The platform focuses on rapid application creation with an emphasis on visual design.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Fast UI generation** : AI-assisted generation of prototypes and user interfaces
- **Backend options** : Database and authentication through Lovable Cloud or a connected Supabase project
- **GitHub sync** : Repository synchronization for working with generated application code
- **Stripe integration** : Payment processing setup through supported integrations
- **Shopify connection** : Native integration for existing Shopify store backends


### **E-commerce Considerations**


Lovable can generate e-commerce frontends quickly, particularly for businesses that want to use Shopify for backend inventory and fulfillment while building custom storefronts. The platform supports creating and refining visual interfaces through conversational prompts. Credit consumption follows a usage-based model where complex debugging sessions can deplete monthly allowances.


Lovable supports mobile-responsive web applications and progressive web apps, but publishing native applications to the App Store or Google Play requires additional packaging solutions.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI development environment from StackBlitz that generates full-stack applications from prompts. The platform operates entirely in the browser without local development setup.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Browser-based development** : Full IDE experience without local installation
- **Live preview** : Instant visualization of generated applications
- **Bolt Cloud** : Managed database, authentication, and hosting services
- **Token-based billing** : Free tier with 1 million tokens monthly and a 300,000-token daily limit
- **Multi-framework support** : React, Vue, and other JavaScript frameworks


### **E-commerce Considerations**


Bolt.new can generate e-commerce applications with database and authentication through Bolt Cloud. The free tier allows experimentation before paid commitment. Token consumption scales with project complexity and iteration cycles. Extended debugging sessions or significant feature additions consume tokens that may exceed monthly allowances during active development periods.


Bolt.new supports JavaScript-centric applications and browser-based development workflows. Businesses should evaluate token consumption, hosting allowances, and application requirements when estimating ongoing costs.


## **4. Replit**


Replit is an established cloud development platform with AI capabilities through Replit Agent. The platform provides a full IDE environment with collaborative features and deployment infrastructure.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Full IDE experience** : Terminal access, file management, and debugging tools
- **Replit Agent** : AI assistant for code generation and modification
- **Collaboration features** : Real-time multiplayer coding and team workspaces
- **Database support** : Managed SQL databases with separate development and production environments
- **Deployment infrastructure** : Hosting with custom domain support


### **E-commerce Considerations**


Replit can build e-commerce applications with full developer control over code and infrastructure choices. The platform suits technical founders who want IDE-level access alongside AI assistance. The platform uses effort-based billing for Agent interactions, where larger tasks can consume more credits.


Replit provides development environment features alongside AI generation capabilities. Businesses seeking detailed control over application code and debugging workflows may find these features useful, although using them can require greater technical familiarity.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 is an AI app builder acquired by Wix in June 2025 for approximately $80 million in initial consideration, plus potential additional earn-out payments. The platform offers quick application generation with managed backend services.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Rapid generation** : Fast application creation from prompts
- **Managed backend** : Database and authentication services included
- **Affordable entry tier** : Starter plan at $16/month billed annually, or $20/month with monthly billing
- **Wix ownership** : Part of Wix following its 2025 acquisition
- **Business tool focus** : Positioning for internal tools and workflows


### **E-commerce Considerations**


Base44 can generate e-commerce applications with its managed backend handling database and authentication requirements. Its Starter plan provides a relatively low-cost entry point. The platform uses a dual credit system with separate allowances for AI messages and integrations. Both credit types reset monthly, requiring usage monitoring to avoid interruptions.


Base44 supports conversational development with managed backend services. Businesses evaluating it for e-commerce should confirm that their required payment integrations, fulfillment processes, and publishing workflows are supported.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual no-code platform with 6 million builders reported in its published figures and more than a decade of market presence. The platform has added AI assistance to its visual builder approach.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual builder** : Drag-and-drop interface for application design
- **Plugin ecosystem** : Extensive plugin library for extended functionality
- **Workflow automation** : Visual logic builder for business processes
- **Bubble AI assistant** : AI-powered assistance for visual building
- **Enterprise features** : Team collaboration and advanced security options


### **E-commerce Considerations**


Bubble provides extensive e-commerce capabilities through its plugin ecosystem, including Stripe, PayPal, and various inventory management integrations. Its established platform supports common e-commerce development patterns. Development speed depends on familiarity with visual building paradigms alongside available AI assistance. Workload unit pricing requires monitoring to predict costs accurately.


Bubble supports both conversational AI assistance and manual visual development. This combination may suit businesses that want direct control over application layouts and workflows.


## **7. Shopify AI**


Shopify has integrated AI capabilities directly into its commerce platform, enabling merchants to generate product descriptions, create marketing content, customize storefronts, and build certain applications using natural language.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Commerce-native AI** : Built into existing Shopify infrastructure
- **Sidekick assistant** : AI assistance for store management and generating custom admin apps
- **Content generation** : Product descriptions and marketing copy
- **Theme customization** : AI-assisted storefront design
- **Existing merchant base** : Millions of businesses worldwide use Shopify


### **E-commerce Considerations**


Shopify AI works within Shopify's established e-commerce infrastructure, where payment processing, inventory management, and fulfillment tools are already available. Shopify Sidekick can generate custom applications for store administration and assist with storefront customization, although generated admin apps operate within Shopify's commerce environment.


Businesses already using Shopify can leverage AI features without platform migration. Those seeking applications outside Shopify's commerce environment may need a separate app-building platform.


## **8. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites is OpenAI's conversational website and lightweight app-building tool, allowing users to create, host, and share interactive web experiences directly through ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Conversational website creation** : Build and refine websites and lightweight applications through natural language prompts
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish sites directly through ChatGPT without configuring separate deployment infrastructure
- **Persistent data storage** : Support for relational database storage and uploaded files
- **User authentication** : Optional sign-in functionality for personalized experiences and saved user data
- **Third-party payments** : Support for commerce experiences using external payment processors
- **Plan-based availability** : Available through eligible paid ChatGPT plans, with building usage limits and hosting overage charges scheduled from January 2027


### **E-commerce Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites can support interactive storefronts, customer-facing tools, and lightweight commerce applications with persistent data and third-party payment integrations. Businesses remain responsible for configuring payment workflows, fulfillment, refunds, and applicable taxes. For more complex e-commerce applications, businesses should evaluate its supported runtime, database options, usage allowances, and deployment limitations before choosing it as their primary platform.


ChatGPT Sites suits users who want to build and publish interactive websites or lightweight commerce applications through conversation. Businesses seeking managed PostgreSQL infrastructure, built-in Stripe payments, and iOS and Android app publishing workflows may also consider Floot alongside their existing AI assistant.


## **Why Floot Stands Out for E-commerce App Building**


Floot combines a full-stack app-building platform with a managed[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) for Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development while Floot provides the infrastructure required to run and publish applications. Available building capabilities depend on the assistant's connector permissions.


For custom e-commerce applications, its capabilities include:


- **Managed database** :[PostgreSQL infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) for product catalogs, customer records, inventory, and order history
- **Payment processing** : Built-in[Stripe integration](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) for checkout, subscriptions, and payment-enabled workflows, with live payments requiring a paid Floot plan and connected Stripe account
- **Authentication and backend** : Customer logins and serverless endpoints for managing orders and business logic
- **Mobile publishing** :[iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) without requiring a Mac or Xcode, with connected developer accounts for store testing
- **SEO and communication** : Optional pre-rendering and page metadata, plus transactional email with paid-plan domain verification and scheduled automation on paid Floot plans


Floot also provides[live chat support](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for setup and troubleshooting. For non-technical founders, this combination reduces the need to configure separate infrastructure services. Building through supported AI connectors uses an existing AI subscription, while Floot plan limits, hosting usage, optional AI credits, and app store requirements still apply.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is an AI app builder and how does it benefit e-commerce businesses?**


An AI app builder translates natural language descriptions into functional application code. For e-commerce, this means describing your store requirements, such as product catalog, shopping cart, and checkout process, and receiving working code rather than building manually. Benefits can include faster development, reduced initial development effort, and the ability for non-technical founders to create custom stores without writing code themselves.


### **Can a fully functional e-commerce app be built without any coding experience using these tools?**


Yes. Platforms like Floot support[non-technical builders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) who describe what they need conversationally. A compatible AI assistant handles code generation while Floot's managed infrastructure handles databases, hosting, and authentication. Stores with product listings, user accounts, shopping carts, and payment processing can be built through conversation rather than manual coding. Businesses should still test payment flows, security, and order processing before launch.


### **What are the typical costs associated with using an AI app builder for an e-commerce platform?**


Costs vary by platform and usage model. Floot's Pro plan at $25/month includes a $10 monthly hosting allowance and 1,000 daily building actions. Token- or credit-based platforms may start at similar prices, but actual costs depend on usage. Factor in your existing Claude, ChatGPT, or other AI subscription when using Floot, alongside potential hosting overages, optional Floot AI credits, payment processing fees, and other third-party service costs.


### **How do AI app builders handle payment processing and user authentication for online stores?**


Most AI builders integrate with payment processors like Stripe and PayPal rather than handling payments directly. Floot provides[built-in Stripe payments](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) , while other payment processors may require custom API integrations. For authentication, Floot includes built-in email/password login and brokers Google/Microsoft OAuth without requiring separate OAuth app registration, simplifying customer account creation.


### **Is it possible to convert a web-based e-commerce app into a mobile app using AI builders?**


Some platforms support this while others focus on web only. Floot packages web applications into iOS and Android apps using native mobile shells. The Pro plan includes 12 mobile builds monthly, with builds running on Floot's infrastructure without requiring a Mac or Xcode. Connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan, and app store approval remains subject to Apple and Google's review processes. Store submission still requires Apple Developer and Google Play developer accounts.
